The petitioners have filed this petition U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming
compensation of Rs.85,00,000/ for the death of Sri.Paramesha K.T, in the road traffic accident
occurred on

sentences.text: 02 . The brief facts are as under: It is submitted that on 19.11.2020 at about 07.20 a.m when the deceased namely Paramesha K.T was proceeding in Honda Moped bearing No.KA52R3789 towards KEB, when he reached in front of Durgasagara hotel, Straight to Ganesha Medicals, BH Road, Nelamangala Town, at that time a container Lorry bearing No.HA38Y6516 driven by its driver in reverse with rash and negligent manner and dashed against the moped of Paramesha and also to the Maruthi Omni Car bearing No.KA52M2850.
Due to this the said Paramesha K.T fell down and the wheel of the container lorry climbed over the body of Paramesha and Maruthi Omni driver Sunil.
As a result both have died at the spot itself.
Then the container hit to the KEB poll.
Then the dead body was shifted to Government hospital, Nelamangala and post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 the petitioners.

Thereafter the petitioners have shifted the dead body in hired vehicle to their native place and conducted funeral and obsequies ceremonies by spending more than Rs.2,00,000/ including transportation, hospitalization charges etc.,.
Due to the death of Paramesha K.T the petitioners being the wife, son and parents have undergone deep mental shock, pain and sufferings, hardship.
That the deceased prior to the accident was hale and healthy and was working at Lorry Transport Office and getting salary of Rs.35,000/ p.m.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of container lorry driver.
Even a criminal case was registered against the container lorry driver.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said container lorry, both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence this petition.

2
03. After service of notice, the respondents have appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.
04. The averments of the written statement of respondent No.1 is as under: This respondent is one of the partner and R.C owner of the goods carrier.
The said goods carrier was (SCCH3) 5 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 duly insured with the respondent No.2 which was valid on the date of accident.

If the court comes to the conclusion that the petitioners are entitled for compensation,
then the respondent No.2 has to indemnify them.
It is false that the husband of petitioner No.1 died due to rash and negligent driving of the goods container.
It is false that the deceased died due to the accidental injuries.
This respondent denied the manner of accident, age, income and dependency.

The claim of the petitioners are excessive and prays to dismiss the petition with costs.
05.

The averments of the written statement of the respondent No.2 is as under : This respondent has issued policy in the name of the respondent No.1 at the time of accident, but liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The goods vehicle driver was not holding valid driving licence on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1 has not intimated about the accident.
The rider of the motorcycle was not wearing helmet and hence he had sustained head injuries.
The deceased was solely responsible for the accident.
Even the rider of motorcycle was not having driving licence.
The petitioners in collusion with the police have filed this (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 false to make unlawful gain.
The petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of the motorcycle were not made as parties.
The goods carrier was falsely implicated in this case.
It is false that the deceased prior to the accident was working at transport office and also doing real estate business and earning Rs.35,000/ p.m.
It is false that due to the death the petitioners have lost love, affection and income.
It is false that the petitioners have spent huge amount towards funeral and transportation expenses.
The claim of the petitioners are excessive and prays to dismiss the petition with costs.
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 was got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 and closed their side.
07. By way of rebuttal, the Assistant Manager of the respondent No.2 was got examined himself as RW.1 and closed their side.

08. Heard arguments from both sides.
09.
Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed:
(SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Paramesha K.T, S/o Timmayya ?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Paramesha K.T, S/o Timmayya died due to the injuries suffered in road traffic accident alleged to have taken place on 19.11.2020 at about 07.15 a.m on Nelamangala Town, BH Road, in front of Ganesh Medicals, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent Smt.Pavitra vs Mahalakshmi Freight Carrier on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11584504/
3 act of driving of the container Lorry bearing reg. No.HR38Y6516 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount & from whom?
04. What order or award?
10. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: Issue No.1 In affirmative Issue No.2 In affirmative Issue No.3 In partly affirmative Issue No.4 As per final order for the following:
REASONS 11. Issues No.1 and 2: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration in order to (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 avoid repetition of facts as they are interrelated with each other.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that the deceased Sri.Paramesha K.T died in road traffic accident which took place on 19.11.2020 due to the rash and negligent driving of container lorry driver.
Further they have contended that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners has lost love and affection and facing hardship.

Hence, they have claimed compensation of Rs.85,00,000/.
12.
Per contra, the same was denied by respondents and stated that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of the container lorry driver but it is due to the negligence of the deceased.
Hence they are not liable to pay the compensation.
13. In order to prove this, the petitioner No.1 was got examined herself as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in her affidavit.
The PW.1 in her crossexamination admitted that "I have not seen the accident.
I do not know the name of person who had lodged complaint to the police.
On the date of accident my husband alone was riding the motorcycle alone.
The motorcycle which my husband was riding (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 belongs to the owner of my husband.
In this accident three vehicles are involved.
It is true that next to accident place there is Durgasagar hotel.
It is true that the front side of motorcycle and back side of lorry are damaged.
It is true that the front side of the car is also damaged.
It is true that in the said BPL card there is no mention of name of my inlaws".
Further the PW.1 had denied all other suggestions of the respondents counsel.
The PW.1 had not seen the accident and she had deposed based on the available documents on record.
14. The PW.1 in support of her case has got marked entire police documents as per Ex.P.1 to 6.

On perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation have filed Charge sheet against the container driver for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC and U/s 122 and 187 of IMV Act.
The concerned I.O has stated that the deceased died only due to the rash and negligent driving of container driver.
Further they have stated that the said container driver after causing the accident did not provide medical aid to the injured and flew from the spot or even not informed to the police.

Smt.Pavitra vs Mahalakshmi Freight Carrier on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11584504/
4 (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 15.
Per contra, the Assistant Manager of the respondent No.2 was got examined himself as RW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the written statement in his affidavit.
The RW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "The company had not issued any authorisation letter to give evidence.
But I am the authorised person.
It is true that our company had issued policy to the offending lorry bearing No. HR38Y6516 subject to terms and conditions.
It is true that as on the date of accident the policy was valid.
We have not challenged the chargesheet filed against lorry driver as we were not party to it".

16. Even the respondents have not produced any documents to show that there is no negligence on part of container driver but the accident took place due to the negligence of the rider of motorcycle only.
It is true that the Rw.1 has not produced any documents to show that he is the authorised person to give evidence on behalf of the respondent No.2.

So it is a irregularity on part of respondent No.2.
17.
So as per Ex.P.1 to 6 it is clear that the concerned I.O has stated that the deceased died at the spot due to the injuries sustained by the container lorry driver with his rash and negligent driving.
The (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 respondent No.1 apart from filing written statement has kept themselves aloof as though they are not connected with this case.
It is true that in Ex.P.6 the IMV report rear left side tail lamp damaged for the container vehicle.
Likewise as per Ex.P.6 front body, headlight indicator, speedometer assembly, rear body handle, chasis brakelights and indicator full body rear side damaged.
Hence it is contended by the respondent No.2 that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased only.
But it is pertinent to note that in this accident three vehicles are involved and even the third vehicle i.e car was also damaged.
It is true that none of the parties have attempted to include the said inmates of the car and its R.C owner and insurer to this case.
18. The respondent No.2 have relied upon decisions reported in a. (2005) 6 SCC 172 - National Insurance Company Limited V/s Prembai Patel and others -

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Prembai Patel and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that the legal heirs of the injured have to establish by preponderance evidence that there was no negligence on part of deceased and he was not responsible for the accident.

(SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.2082/2021  b. 2014 AIR SCW 1081 - Lachoo Ram and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation - It is observed that mere involvement of vehicle in accident cannot make respondent liable to pay compensation unless it is shown that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent of that driver.

entities.text: AIR SCW 1081 - Lachoo Ram and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: c. 2012 AIR SCW 2241 - Surinder Kumar Arora and another V/s Dr.Manoj Bisla and others -

entities.text: Surinder Kumar Arora and another V/s Dr.Manoj Bisla and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that the onus to prove the act of rash and negligent driving by driver of vehicle was on claimants.

Smt.Pavitra vs Mahalakshmi Freight Carrier on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11584504/
5 19.
It is true that the claimants who have approached this court have to prove that there was no negligence on part of deceased/injured.
In the instant case with the available records the petitioners have proved that the husband of petitioner No.1 died at the spot due to the accidental injuries caused by the container lorry driver.
The respondent No.2 have not proved the alleged negligence by the deceased for the accident.
Hence the above preposition is not helpful to the respondent No.2.
So merely on basis of IMV report by excluding other police records it cannot be said that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased only.

Even the respondent No.1 of the RW.1 have not lodge complaint to the police or before any (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 authority to show that the container lorry driver was not negligent or responsible for the accident.
Hence there is no supportive documents on behalf of the respondents to show that the deceased is responsible for the accident.
So with the available documents on record it is true that the container lorry driver was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and it caused accident.
It is true that the respondents have not challenged the chargesheet filed against the container lorry driver.

20. Further the petitioners in order to prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased have produced and got marked the notarized copies of their Aadhaar cards, bank pass books, PAN card, Driving licence of deceased as per Ex.P.8 to 18 and 20.
There is no serious dispute with regard to relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
It is true that the petitioners are the wife, children and parents of the deceased.
Hence the petitioners being the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased are entitled for the compensation.
Hence I answered the issues No.1 and 2 in affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
As per above findings, it is clear that the accident took place due to the negligence (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 of container lorry driver.

The petitioners being the dependents of deceased are entitled for compensation as under:
a) Loss of dependency:-
The petitioners have stated that deceased was 34 years at the time of accident.
In this regard the PW.1 has got marked Aadhaar card and Driving licence of deceased as per Ex.P.7 and 18 which shows the deceased was born in the year 1986 and the accident took place on 19.11.2020.
So it is just and proper to consider the age of the deceased as 34 years at the time of accident for calculating the compensation.
As per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the proper applicable multiplier is "16" and the same is considered.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have got marked the employment letter as per Ex.P.19 wherein it is stated that the deceased was working as employer from 10.01.2020 to 19.11.2020 and was getting salary.
In support of Ex.P.19 the PW.1 has not produced any other documents to show that the deceased was working under NUCO Transport and getting salary.
Further the Ex.P.20 is the account (SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 statement of the deceased and it shown there is no fixed salary disbursed to the deceased.
Even the petitioners have not examined the author of Ex.P.19.
Hence the stated income of the deceased could not be considered.
Under these circumstances it is just and proper to consider the notional income of the deceased.
The date of accident is on 19.11.2020 and the notional income for the said year comes to Rs.14,500/ per month.

Smt.Pavitra vs Mahalakshmi Freight Carrier on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11584504/
6

As aforesaid the deceased has four dependents i.e wife, son and parents and as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 if the dependents are 4 to 6, then personal deduction is to be 1/4th.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in this case 1/4th deduction has to be done towards personal expenses.
So, after deduction of 1/4th income (Rs.3,625/), then the income comes to Rs.10,875/.
Further as per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in National Insurance Company Ltd.,
V/s Pranay Sethi case reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 the petitioners are entitled for future prospects as the deceased is aged about 34 years at the time of his death.
The deceased being the self employed and (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 comes within the age group of below 40 years, an 40% of income (Rs.4,350/) to be added towards future prospects.
Hence the income for calculation comes to Rs.15,225/ per month.

Hence the petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,225 x 12 x 16 =
Rs.29,23,200/ under this head.
b) Loss of estate and funeral expenses:

Since it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd.,
Vs Pranay Sethi and others case in AIR 2017 SC 5157 that the dependents would be entitled for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/ and funeral expenses to the extent of Rs.15,000/,
as such I award the same.
c) Loss of consortium:

In this case the petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/ towards spousal consortium, the petitioner No.2 being the son and the petitioners No.3 and 4 being the parents are entitled for Rs.40,000/ each towards parental and filial consortium as per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors case and (SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 Magma General Insurance Company case in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence I award the same.

22. Thus the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1.Loss of dependency Rs.29,23,200/
2.Loss of estate 15,000/
3.Towards spousal consortium 40,000/ (for the petitioner No.1)
4.Towards parental consortium 40,000/ (for the petitioner No.2)
5.Towards filial consortium (for 80,000/ the petitioners No.3 and 4)
6.Funeral expenses 15,000/ Total Rs.31,13,200/
23.
Regarding liability:
As stated above the petitioners have proved that the deceased namely Sri.Paramesha K.T died due to accidental injuries caused due to rash and negligent driving of container driver.
Hence the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said container are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence,

7 issue No.3 is answered in partly Affirmative.
(SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 24. Issue No.4:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3 as above the petitioners have proved their case.
With regard to apportionment of compensation the petitioner No.1 being the wife and manager of the family is entitled for 50% of the award amount.
The petitioner No.2 being the minor son is entitled for 30% of the award amount.
The petitioners No.3 and 4 being the parents of the deceased are entitled for 10% each of the award amount.
25. Further with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioners are entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
As such I proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec 166 of the M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part, with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for Rs.31,13,200/ (Thirty one lakhs thirteen thousand two hundred only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However - in view of holding valid insurance the respondent No.2 shall deposit the amount within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest accrued, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for 50%, the petitioner No.2 is entitled for 30% of the award amount and petitioners No.3 and 4 are entitled for 10% each of the award amount.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest accrued, an 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner No.1 in any nationalized bank or schedule bank for a period of three years of her choice and the remaining amount shall be released to her through E payment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
However, PW.1 is at liberty to withdraw periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest accrued, entire amount shall be kept as FD in any nationalized bank in the name of petitioner (SCCH3) 20 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 No.2 on his choice of petitioner No.1 till he attains age of majority.
However the petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the interest and to make use for the welfare of the petitioner No.2 only.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest accrued, entire amount shall be released in the name of the petitioners No.3 and 4 through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

(SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.2082/2021  b. 2014 AIR SCW 1081 - Lachoo Ram and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation - It is observed that mere involvement of vehicle in accident cannot make respondent liable to pay compensation unless it is shown that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent of that driver.
c. 2012 AIR SCW 2241 - Surinder Kumar Arora and another V/s Dr.Manoj Bisla and others -
In the instant case with the available records the petitioners have proved that the husband of petitioner No.1 died at the spot due to the accidental injuries caused by the container lorry driver.
The respondent No.2 have not proved the alleged negligence by the deceased for the accident.
So merely on basis of IMV report by excluding other police records it cannot be said that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased only.
Even the respondent No.1 of the RW.1 have not lodge complaint to the police or before any (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 authority to show that the container lorry driver was not negligent or responsible for the accident.
Hence there is no supportive documents on behalf of the respondents to show that the deceased is responsible for the accident.
So with the available documents on record it is true that the container lorry driver was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and it caused accident.
There is no serious dispute with regard to relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Hence the petitioners being the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased are entitled for the compensation.
The petitioners being the dependents of deceased are entitled for compensation as under:
a) Loss of dependency:-
So it is just and proper to consider the age of the deceased as 34 years at the time of accident for calculating the compensation.
As per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the proper applicable multiplier is "16" and the same is considered.
In order to prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have got marked the employment letter as per Ex.P.19 wherein it is stated that the deceased was working as employer from 10.01.2020 to 19.11.2020 and was getting salary.
In support of Ex.P.19 the PW.1 has not produced any other documents to show that the deceased was working under NUCO Transport and getting salary.
Further the Ex.P.20 is the account (SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.2082/2021 statement of the deceased and it shown there is no fixed salary disbursed to the deceased.
Even the petitioners have not examined the author of Ex.P.19.
Hence the stated income of the deceased could not be considered.
Under these circumstances it is just and proper to consider the notional income of the deceased.
The date of accident is on 19.11.2020 and the notional income for the said year comes to Rs.14,500/ per month.
